;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
**[[Armenia–Russia relations]]
***[[Prime Minister of Armenia|Armenian Prime Minister]] [[Nikol Pashinyan]] formally requests "urgent consultations on providing security" to [[Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] amid its escalating conflict with [[Azerbaijan]] in disputed [[Nagorno-Karabakh]] that has left thousands dead. [[Russia]] says it would provide "necessary" assistance to [[Armenia]] without alluding further. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20201031-armenia-requests-russia-s-help-after-no-new-trucein-nagorno-karabakh-conflict (France 24)]
**Videos emerge allegedly showing [[Azerbaijani Armed Forces]] using [[white phosphorus munitions]] on forested areas in Nagorno-Karabakh, although Azerbaijan's [[Ministry of Defence (Azerbaijan)|Ministry of Defence]] denies the use of white phosphorus. [https://tass.com/world/1218643 (TASS)] [https://www.almasdarnews.com/article/azerbaijani-forces-use-white-phosphorus-over-karabakh-video/ (Al Masdar News)]
*[[Kivu conflict]]; [[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**[[2020 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks]]
***[[Allied Democratic Forces]] militants kills 21 civilians in an attack on a village in the village of Lisasa, [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. More people were kidnapped, a health centre was ransacked, while homes were set on fire and a Catholic church desecrated. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/31/21-dead-in-new-dr-congo-massacre-by-adf-rebel-group-official (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Iraqi insurgency (2017–present)|Iraqi insurgency]]
**Two children are killed and 28 wounded in a bombing targeting a [[gas pipeline]] in [[Muthanna Governorate]], [[Iraq]]. It is the second time this week that an oil facility has been targeted. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/10/31/Gas-pipeline-blast-in-Iraq-kills-2-injures-51 (Al Arabiya English)]
*[[2020 Nigeria hostage rescue]] 
**[[SEAL Team Six]] conducts a predawn raid in northern [[Nigeria]], rescuing [[Americans|American]] hostage Philip Walton, who was kidnapped in [[Niger]]. [[The Pentagon]] says no [[U.S. military]] personnel were injured in the operation. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/seal-team-6-rescues-us-citizen-philip-walton-nigeria/ (CBS News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Pacific typhoon season]]
**[[Typhoon Goni (2020)|Typhoon Goni]]
***[[government of the Philippines|Philippine authorities]] in [[Luzon Island|Luzon]] order the evacuation of thousands as Goni approaches as a [[category 5 storm]], the world's strongest this year. Ten people are killed by the typhoon. [https://www.reuters.com/article/BigStory12/idUSKBN27H0YY (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Aegean Sea earthquake]]
**The death toll of the [[earthquake]] that struck [[Greece]] and [[Turkey]] yesterday rises to 39, as 17 more people are found dead in [[Izmir]]. Rescue teams in the city are hunting through the rubble of collapsed buildings for survivors. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/10/31/europe/earthquake-turkey-greece-aegean-sea-rescue-scli-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]]
*****[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] announces a month-long nationwide [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] in [[England]]. The new rules are to come into effect at midnight on November 5 and will last until December 2. However, unlike the first lockdown in March, schools, colleges and universities can stay open and major sporting events will go ahead as normal. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-54763956 (BBC News)]
****The [[United Kingdom]] surpasses one million cases of COVID-19. [https://news.sky.com/story/coronavirus-confirmed-covid-19-cases-in-the-uk-surpass-one-million-mark-12119871 (Sky News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Austria]], [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns]]
****[[Chancellor of Austria|Chancellor]] [[Sebastian Kurz]] announces a "second lockdown" that orders bars and restaurants to close except for deliveries and takeout and imposes a nighttime curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. local time beginning November 2 and lasting for four weeks. [https://www.oe24.at/oesterreich/politik/lockdown-in-oesterreich-gilt-ab-dienstag-0-uhr/452287788 (OE24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] reports a record 19,059 new cases and surpasses 500,000 cumulative cases, according to data from the [[Robert Koch Institute]], making it the fourth consecutive time the country sets a new record of daily infections. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/europe/covid-19-cases-in-germany-surpasses-500000/articleshow/78964465.cms (''The Times of India'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]], [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns]]
****[[Prime Minister of Greece|Prime Minister]] [[Kyriakos Mitsotakis]] declares a one-month partial lockdown in [[Athens]] and other major cities beginning next week. Under the rules, restaurants, bars and gyms would be closed beginning November 3. However, in contrast to the first lockdown, travel within the country will not be affected and schools and shops will remain open. In the rest of the country, masks will become mandatory and a curfew will be imposed from midnight to 5:00 a.m. local time. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/258682/article/ekathimerini/news/new-restrictions-in-effect-for-november (''Ekathimerini'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****The number of new infections in [[Hungary]] surges by a record 3,908 in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide cases total to 75,321. [https://dailynewshungary.com/coronavirus-in-hungary-number-of-infections-up-by-a-record-3908/ (Daily News Hungary)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] reports 31,758 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-italy-idUKKBN27G0UK (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland]] reports a record 21,897 new cases, bringing the total number of cases since the beginning of the [[pandemic]] to 362,731. [https://polandin.com/50573520/covid19-recordbreaking-21629-new-infections-in-poland (Poland In)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Government of Portugal|Portuguese government]] reimposes a partial lockdown from 4 November affecting the 70% of the national territory. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-portugal-idUKKBN27G0V8 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 8,752 new infections in the last 24 hours, raising its cumulative case total to 387,481. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/covid-19-in-ukraine-8752-new-cases-155-deaths-221357-active-cases.html (''Kyiv Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
****[[Michigan]] reports 3,792 new cases, a new single-day record. [https://www.clickondetroit.com/health/2020/10/31/michigan-coronavirus-cases-up-to-178180-death-toll-now-at-7340/ (WDIV-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
****[[Governor of New York|Governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] announces that travelers outside of the [[New York metropolitan area|New York metro area]] will be required to undergo mandatory [[COVID-19 testing|testing]]. [https://www.nydailynews.com/coronavirus/ny-coronavirus-cuomo-mandatory-testing-rulles-20201031-vq6ihu7zkvfgnod4f5oikvklae-story.html (''New York Daily News'')] [https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/coronavirus/cuomo-ditches-quarantine-list-for-sweeping-ny-entry-test-policy/2697913/ (WNBC-TV)]
***A study by [[Stanford University]] reports over 30,000 new cases and 700 deaths from COVID-19 have been linked to [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s [[List of post–2016 election Donald Trump rallies|campaign rallies]]. [https://www.latimes.com/science/story/2020-10-31/super-spreading-trump-rallies-led-to-more-than-700-covid-19-deaths-study (''Los Angeles Times'')]
*[[Environmental dumping]]
**[[Sri Lanka]] begins shipping back 242 [[Intermodal container|containers]] of [[hazardous waste]] to the United Kingdom, after a Sri Lankan court ruled two weeks ago that their importation violated local and international shipping regulations. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/2011647/sri-lanka-sends-waste-back-to-uk (''Bangkok Post'')] 

;Law and crime
*[[2020 Lyon shooting]]
**A [[Greek Orthodox]] [[priest]] is critically wounded after being shot twice while closing his church in [[Lyon]], [[France]]. The attacker fled the scene. The victim, a [[Greeks|Greek]] national, is being treated for life-threatening injuries. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54763136 (BBC News)]
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]]
**[[Kenosha unrest]], [[Kenosha unrest shooting]], [[George Floyd protests]]
***[[Illinois]] authorities announce that Kyle Rittenhouse, the 17-year-old boy accused of fatally shooting two demonstrators in [[Kenosha, Wisconsin|Kenosha]], [[Wisconsin]], will be [[extradite]]d to stand trial on [[homicide]] charges. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/illinois-authorities-extradite-kyle-rittenhouse-to-wisconsin/2020/10/30/96df4102-1b0c-11eb-8bda-814ca56e138b_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[Killing of Walter Wallace]]
***Protesters gather in [[West Philadelphia]] to protest the [[Philadelphia Police Department|police]] killing of Walter Wallace Jr. [https://whyy.org/articles/west-philly-rally-resumes-protest-against-police-killing-of-walter-wallace-jr/ (WHYY-TV)]
*[[2019–2021 Iraqi protests]]
**Iraqi security forces clear the camps set up by protesters in [[Baghdad]]'s [[Liberation Square, Baghdad|Tahrir Square]] and re-open a major bridge that connects to the [[Green Zone]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/31/iraq-clears-tahrir-square-a-year-after-mass-protests-began (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Quebec City stabbing]]
**Two people are killed and five others are injured in a series of stabbings in [[Quebec City]], [[Quebec]], Canada. The suspect, a man in his 20s who was wearing medieval-style armor, is now in police custody. [https://globalnews.ca/news/7435389/quebec-city-stabbing-bladed-weapon/ (Global News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Elections in Australia]]
**[[2020 Queensland state election]]
***Incumbent [[Premier of Queensland|Premier]] [[Annastacia Palaszczuk]]'s [[Australian Labor Party (Queensland Branch)|Labor Party]] expands their majority in the election. Palaszczuk becomes the first woman to win three elections in [[History of Australia|Australian history]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-11-01/qld-state-election-labor-wins-annastacia-palaszczuk-elected/12834982 (ABC)]
*[[2020 Tanzanian general election]]
**Opposition parties say that they will not recognize the election's result, which gave incumbent [[President of Tanzania|President]] [[John Magufuli]] another term. The [[Chadema]] party calls for fresh elections. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tanzania-politics/tanzanias-two-leading-opposition-parties-reject-poll-demand-new-vote-idUSKBN27G0DM?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Ivorian presidential election]]
**[[Ivorians]] head to the polls to elect their [[President of Ivory Coast|President]]. Incumbent [[Alassane Ouattara]] seeks a third term, while main opposition candidates [[Pascal Affi N'Guessan]] and [[Henri Konan Bédié]] say it is illegal for Ouattara to seek a third term and have boycotted the election and called for [[civil disobedience]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-54733425 (BBC News)]
*[[2020 Georgian parliamentary election]]
**Voters in [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] head to the polls to elect the members of the country's [[Parliament of Georgia (country)|parliament]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/georgian-opposition-unites-in-bid-to-oust-billionaire-backed-party/a-55455591 (DW)]
